newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SUPER MARIO SCORES FOUR TIMES IN THIRD PERIOD IN PENS' WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SUPER MARIO SCORES FOUR TIMES IN THIRD PERIOD IN PENS' WIN.

text.p: Mario Lemieux tied an NHL record by scoring four times in the third period, leading the Pittsburgh Penguins to a 5-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens Sunday.
Lemiuex's 10th career four-goal game gave the Penguins their first win in Montreal since 1988.

Lemieux's effort marked the 11th time in league history that a player has scored four times in a period, and the fifth time it has been done in the final stanza. Washington's Peter Bondra was the last player with four in a period, scoring four times in the first against Tampa Bay on February 5, 1994.

Lemieux broke his own team record for goals in a period, finishing the burst by sending the puck from his own zone into an empty net with the Penguins shorthanded and 1:31 left. He is second in the league with 34 goals and leads the NHL with 84 points.
The Penguins were 0-2-11 in Montreal since October 29, 1988, but Lemieux, who has not performed well in his career against the Canadiens in his home town, took over in the third.

"It may not have been the best game of my career, but certainly the best match I've played in Montreal," Lemieux said. "It's very special what I did out there today because I haven't played well in Montreal."

"We were aware of our jinx here in Montreal," Penguins coach Ed Johnston said. "I went in the dressing room before the third period and said, 'We haven't won here in a long time so let's play solid in the third.' Montreal gives us fits. We always seem to bring the best out of Montreal."
Lemieux helped the Penguins stop a two-game losing streak and improve to 13-2-2 in their last 17 games.
"I was laughing at myself because I missed so many early chances in the game," said Lemieux. "I knew sooner or later something would happen."

Pittsburgh's rookie goaltender Patrick Lalime made 42 saves as he shook off consecutive defeats following the record 14-0-2 streak that started his career. He stopped All-Star Game Most Valuable Player Mark Recchi on consecutive breakaways midway through the second period to preserve what was then a 1-1 tie.

"Those two stops I made on Recchi helped me win the game," said Lalime, a native of St. Bonaventure, Quebec, near Quebec City. "Losing the last two games before this one didn't challenge my confidence. I was nervous with all my friends and family here. I'm happy I played a great game."
"The key to the game was when Lalime stopped Recchi on both of those breakaways," Johnston said.
Jason Woolley added a power-play goal for Pittsburgh, which is 6-0-1 in its last seven road games and 12-1-1 in its last 14 away from home after opening the season 0-11-1 on the road.
David Wilkie and Sebastien Bordeleau scored for Montreal, which suffered its third straight loss -- getting outscored 19-4 -- and fell to 2-6 in its last eight. It was Bordeleau's first NHL goal.

"We played a lot better today than yesterday," Canadiens coach Mario Tremblay said. "The difference today, though, was Lalime and Lemieux. Now we know why Lemieux is the best player in hockey. There's no sense in Mario saying he's going to retire after this year, I can't see it.
"When Recchi missed those two breakaways and the score was only 1-1, the game sort of turned around."
"Mario had a lot of good chances today, but Mario is Mario, he can turn a whole game around because he has lots of jump," Johnston said. "Only Mario can turn a game around like he did."

Pittsburgh's Jaromir Jagr aggravated a recurring ankle injury late in the game, but it is not believed to be serious. Teammate Fredrik Olausson sustained a broken cheekbone when he was hit by a shot from Montreal's Stephane Quintal. He might be able to play with a facemask.
Montreal winger Martin Rucinsky re-injured a separated shoulder. He will make the trip to Florida but might not play in Tuesday's game.
At Washington, Daniel McGillis scored twice, including the go-ahead goal 4:53 into the third period, to lift the Edmonton Oilers to a 3-1 victory over the Capitals.
McGillis, who has three goals over Edmonton's last two games but only five this season, celebrated his first career two-goal game and helped the Oilers complete their road trip at 2-1-1.
Todd Marchant added a late insurance goal and Curtis Joseph made 40 saves for the Oilers (23-22-5), 4-1-1 in their last six games.
"I'm tired of giving the opposing goaltenders credit," Capitals coach Jim Schoenfeld said. "It seems we make a lot of them first stars."
Peter Bondra scored a power-play goal, his 30th of the season, for Washington, which has lost three straight.
